Orthogonal spectral decomposition reduces the squared residual ratio to a normalized fourth central moment. Convexity makes the two spectral endpoints extremal at fixed mean, yielding the exact one-variable envelope. Strict monotonicity in \(\kappa\), Descartes uniqueness for the reciprocal threshold polynomial, and the exact rational witness were reconstructed and checked. value.rationale: Wild CGS residual oscillations are a long-recognized practical defect that motivated smoother product Krylov methods. The finding gives the defect a sharp, reusable quantitative boundary in the simplest well-conditioned setting: below \(\kappa_*=3.442815869257\ldots\) the first residual cannot grow for any SPD problem, above it a two-dimensional diagonal problem already forces growth, and the sharp worst spike scales as \(\kappa^{3/2}\). This identifies exactly when the first CGS squaring step ceases to be norm-safe and quantifies how severe the loss can become.
